decisions.reason: The unspecified boundary-approximation index inherited the zero-based convention, making 1/n undefined at zero. This is a nonfatal indexing defect: the continuous datum itself has a Poisson extension, and using phi_n=u+1/(n+1), n>=0, gives h_n=H+1/(n+1) and inf h_n=H. Also made the p<1 Jensen argument explicitly use convex -t^(p/q) with integrable input and composition, and supplied continuity at radius zero. The Statement is unchanged; no consumer propagation is required.

False positive: the Definition explicitly supplies (a_n)_(n>=1), not a function with an additional zero-th term. Its sums, product, partial products and supplier thm-hardy-zero-set-blaschke-condition consistently use that positive-indexed domain; reindex f_k=b_(a_(k+1)), k>=0, to apply the normal-product theorem. The proposed a_0=0 is not a term of the supplied sequence. The compact summable-defect bound includes a=0 separately, ensures finitely many origin factors and gives the expected zeros. No item edit is warranted.

The arbitrary-holomorphic outer equivalence was attributed to lem-outer-function-properties(iv), which assumes h in Lp and g in Hp; neither is supplied in this Definition. The same mismatch affected its unconditional holomorphy assertion. This is a fatal dependency-citation gap at the declared unrestricted interface, not a false equivalence. Repaired by deriving the logarithmic kernel integral as a convergent power series for every L1 logarithmic datum, citing entire exponential and its modulus identity, and proving both equivalence directions directly using the constant-modulus quotient and published maximum principle. The Lp/Hardy and boundary conclusions remain cited only with their actual hypotheses; no claim is weakened.

L3 omitted integrability of t, required by both cited Jensen interfaces. For t(s)=-1/s on (0,1), e^t is integrable but the real expectation of t is not defined. This is nonfatal for the lemma: its actual application t=p log h is integrable because log h is L1 and the fixed Poisson kernel is bounded; h^p is likewise integrable against that weight. Repaired L3 to state both weighted integrability hypotheses and step 2.1 to verify them explicitly, with a finite representative on null exceptional sets. Added direct entire-exponential and modulus-identity dependencies to license L2 and the modulus computation. All four Statement clauses are unchanged and their series, Jensen/Tonelli, CC boundary-limit and constant-quotient arguments remain valid.

downstream_reviews.snippet:
Equivalently, $N^+(\mathbb D)$ is the class of quotients $g/h$ with
$g,h\in H^\infty(\mathbb D)$ and $h$ outer (and then $h$ may be normalized by
$h(0)>0$); this equivalence is proved in
[[lem-smirnov-class-quotient-characterisation]]. The class $N^+$ is a complex vector space, as certified using the quotient characterization just proved by [[lem-smirnov-class-quotient-characterisation]], its `justified_by` supplier. Indeed, for nonzero $f_j=g_j/h_j$ with bounded holomorphic numerators and bounded outer denominators, $h_1h_2$ is bounded and outer: its boundary logarithm is the sum of the two integrable boundary logarithms, and its interior log-modulus is their Poisson integral by linearity, in the outer convention of [[def-inner-singular-inner-and-outer-functions]]. Thus $f_1+f_2=(g_1h_2+g_2h_1)/(h_1h_2)$ has bounded numerator and bounded outer denominator. If the numerator is zero, the sum is the already included zero function; otherwise the characterization gives membership in $N^+$. Scalar multiplication uses the same denominator and numerator $cg_j$, including $c=0$. This certification is not used in the proof of the quotient characterization, which depends only on the displayed defining inequality.

downstream_reviews.snippet: [L3] If $H\ge0$ has $\log H\in L^1$, the outer function $[H]$ is holomorphic and zero-free, with $\log|[H]|=P[\log H]$ and $[H](0)=\exp(\int\log H)>0$. In particular, for $\varphi\ge0$ in $L^1$, $h=[e^{-\varphi}]$ satisfies $\log|h|=-P[\varphi]\le0$, hence $|h|\le1$. Products of bounded outer functions remain bounded and outer, by adding their integrable boundary logarithms and their Poisson log-modulus identities. ([[lem-outer-function-properties]], [[def-inner-singular-inner-and-outer-functions]])

downstream_reviews.snippet: [L5] For a nonzero finite positive singular measure $\mu$, $S_\mu$ is zero-free, $|S_\mu|\le1$, $S_\mu(0)=e^{-\mu(\mathbb T)}<1$, and $|S_\mu^*|=1$ almost everywhere under CC. Its reciprocal is holomorphic with $\log|1/S_\mu|=P[\mu]\ge0$, hence belongs to N. If the reciprocal were bounded, its boundary modulus one and the CC bounded-holomorphic norm identity would force $|1/S_\mu|\le1$, contradicting $1/S_\mu(0)>1$. Thus it is not bounded; no divergence claim at every support point is required. ([[thm-singular-inner-function-properties]], [[lem-bounded-holomorphic-disc-functions-have-fatou-limits-under-countable-choice]], [[def-inner-singular-inner-and-outer-functions]], [[thm-nevanlinna-boundary-values-and-log-integrability]])
